title: Soft-cancel signal and timed reconnect window for OpenAI-compat streaming
author: Priya Menon
release_notes: Introduces a soft-cancel client signal and a bounded reconnect/resume window for OpenAI-compatible streaming sessions. Improves graceful disconnect handling and reduces inadvertent cold restarts. No public API breaking changes; opt-in fields for compat layer.
description:
Context and motivation:
Clients and downstream SDKs have been filing incidents where a transient network disconnect or accidental client-side cancel caused a hard termination of a server-side generation mid-critical-tool invocation. This leads to duplicated side-effects when clients retry and poor UX for long-running tool calls. ENG-1842 asked for a safer, backward-compatible streaming lifecycle control that: (1) gives the client a soft-cancel option to request an early but safe end-of-stream, (2) provides a short, server-backed reconnect/resume window so clients can reconnect and resume without restarting the model state, and (3) tightens server-side eviction policy to avoid resource leakage.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a client-visible soft-cancel signal that the OpenAI-compat adapter accepts as "soft_cancel": true in the stream preamble; server treats this as a hint to stop producing new tool invocations, flush structured outputs, and close streams at a safe cutpoint rather than an immediate hard abort.
- Implements a timed resume window (resume_window_ms, default 30_000ms) with short-lived resume tokens returned in the stream termination envelope. A reconnect within the window with the resume token allows the connection manager to rehydrate KV cache and continue where possible.
- Updates server eviction to maintain ephemeral session metadata for the resume window; sessions are aggressively garbage-collected after window expiry.
- Preserves structured output and function-calling semantics across soft-cancel+resume boundaries. If a function call was in-flight, we mark it as 'incomplete' in the termination envelope and allow SDKs to decide whether to re-run.
- Adds observability: new metrics (stream_soft_cancel_total, stream_resume_attempts, stream_resume_success) and alert tweaks to avoid noisy paging for expected reconnects.

Commits (summary):
- ae3f2b9  add: resume token envelope and resume_window_ms handling in openai_compat adapter
- 4b7d0c1  feat: connection manager: keep ephemeral session metadata for resume window
- d98a79e  fix: ensure KV cache rehydration only for compatible model variants
- 0c2a5f4  feat(sdk/ts): streaming client handshake for soft_cancel + resume token
- b5c3a11  test: stream_simulator integration test for disconnect+resume race
- f7a1d2e  docs: openai_compat streaming docs + migration section

Files changed (high level):
- pkg/stream/connection_manager.go: new session store layer (ephemeral TTL), resume token validation, metrics hooks. Small new helper ~180 LOC.
- pkg/stream/protocol/openai_compat.go: parsing of soft_cancel in preamble, termination envelope with resume token/resume_window_ms, compatibility handling for older clients.
- pkg/stream/heartbeat.go: improved heartbeat to update last-seen for resume window and to emit resume candidate metrics.
- sdk/typescript/src/streaming.ts: handshake additions, client option softCancel(), automatic small-retry for reconnect-with-resume.
- docs/openai_compat/streaming.md: new section describing soft-cancel semantics and examples for SDKs.
- internal/testing/stream_simulator.go: adds simulate-flaky-network and reconnect-with-resume scenario for CI.
- console/alerts/stream-timeouts.json: tuned thresholds and one-shot suppression window to avoid paging on expected transient reconnects.
- charts/streaming/values.yaml: minimal default for resume_window_ms and metric configs.

Compatibility notes:
- The soft-cancel field is optional; older clients will ignore it. Servers that do not opt-in to resume_window_ms behave as before (hard termination). The OpenAI-compat adapter will only emit resume tokens when resume_window_ms > 0. No breaking API changes.

Testing and CI:
- Unit test matrix added for 3 model variants and various sequence lengths.
- Stream_simulator integration test initially exposed a flake where KV cache rehydration raced with model warmup (failing test in CI run #1). Fix applied (d98a79e) and CI stabilized.
- CI checks: go-unit, go-integration, ts-unit, lint, e2e-stream-sim. Final run: all passing.

Review thread (selected):
- Yara: "Can we add a metric that tags resume failures by failure reason (token-expired/model-mismatch)? Also please ensure the termination envelope doesn't leak internal IDs."
- Author (Priya): "Added resume_failure_reason tag and redacted internal IDs in the termination envelope (see ae3f2b9). Also updated docs to call out best practices for retries."
- Carlos: "Nits: rename resume_window_ms -> resume_window_ms to be explicit on units (ms). Add a small comment on expected cost model for holding ephemeral sessions."
- Eliot: "Integration test looks comprehensive; recommend small timeout increase on sim to reduce flakiness in CI."
- Carlos: "Approved after nit fixes."

CI timeline and actions:
- 2026-02-12 08:11 UTC: CI run #1 (go unit/integration) - e2e-stream-sim failed due to KV rehydration race.
- 2026-02-12 10:02 UTC: Patch (d98a79e) landed to gate rehydration on warmup signal.

Merge outcome:
- Squash-merged into main on 2026-02-15 by main-bot. Changelog entry added under release-candidate. No rollout guard required; feature behind opt-in config flag resume_window_ms > 0.

Migration guidance for SDKs and clients:
- SDKs should surface an opt-in softCancel() option and expose resume token storage for short-lived reconnections. The TS SDK change included here demonstrates the minimal handshake; server will ignore unknown preamble keys for older clients.

Follow-ups captured in ENG-1917:
- Dashboard for resume success rate and per-customer resume latency.
- SRE runbook for investigating resume failures and recommended escalation thresholds.

If revert is needed: the opt-in flag means a quick config rollback (resume_window_ms -> 0) will restore previous behavior without any state migration.

References: ENG-1842 (design doc link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1842/soft-cancel-and-resume-window-design), internal perf notes and console dashboard PR linked in the design doc.
